description: The AAS journals' class, AASTeX 7.0.1 (CTAN's copy, in case the mirror's snapshot predates it). Its preamble (round 2 of batch 1, GitHub run 41584963423) redefines three of the class's footnote macros, copied from the pinned aastex701.cls with two changes. (1) \make@footnotetext (l.527-541) adds \vadjust{\vskip\z@skip} after the footnote's last line only in horizontal mode. footnotehyper, which General's footnotes load, releases its saved notes through the class's \@footnotetext with \@makefntext, \@finalstrut and \rule emptied, so the \vadjust came after \unvbox in internal vertical mode: 'You can't use \vadjust in internal vertical mode' in every General footnote (F19: 1,547 not-denied branches, 1,179 failing on nothing else; 16 cells ended at TeX's 100-error stop). In horizontal mode, where every footnote of the class's own path ends, it is unchanged. (2) \@makefntext (l.7567-7569) and \@mpmakefntext (l.6209-6215, footnotes in floats and minipages) take paragraphs (\long), as the kernel's and revtex4-2's aps4-2.rtx \@makefntext do: General's block footnotes stopped at 'Paragraph ended before \@makefntext was complete' (F31: 596 branches; F49: 114 more, whose runaway argument ran to the end of the file). A footnote without a paragraph break sets as before. (3) The class's preamble builder relaxes \@endpbox, \do@row@strut and \ar@align@mcell (b22, owner item JR2-2), as array's own \@mkpream does (array.sty 2026/02/24 v2.7b l.432-434) and the class's older \@mkpream@array did (l.1376). aastex701 loads array itself (l.8716) and at \begin{document} swaps in revtex4-2's copies of its internals (\switch@array, l.760, l.883-955); their \@mkpream@array@new (l.1401-1454) calls \@mkpream@relax (l.1366-1373, 1455-1463), which relaxes \@startpbox but not \@endpbox. array adds each p-column with \xdef (\@addtopreamble, array.sty l.55), so the class's \@endpbox (\@finalstrut\@arstrutbox\color@endgroup\egroup\hfil, l.8721) was expanded while the preamble was built, and the kernel's \color@endgroup (\endgraf\ifvmode\@endpefalse\fi\endgroup, latex.ltx l.16353) tested the mode then: in vertical mode \@endpefalse expands the conditional \if@endpe inside the \xdef, which takes the \fi of \ifvmode, so the \or ending the p-column case raised 'Extra \or' (...\@endpbox \do@row@strut \or) and every later \or of \@mkpream's \ifcase repeated it until TeX's 100-error stop. In the GitHub run every tabularx begun in vertical mode (General's tables at the top level, in a [H] table, first in a statement, in vwcol's measuring \parbox) stopped there: 317 aastex cells, 21 of 21 such tables reached with no earlier error in a sample of 75 aastex.A cells, while 27 of 27 begun after \leavevmode or \noindent built cleanly (in the horizontal mode \ifvmode skipped \@endpefalse). Relaxed, \@endpbox stays a token in the preamble and runs in its cell, as in every class that loads array, so the build no longer depends on the mode, and tabularx and colortbl stay fit here though revtex4-2 refuses them for the same swap. A cell that ends in vertical mode (General's cells end with \par) now ends as array ends it: \@finalstrut takes back the line its strut starts (\vskip-\baselineskip) instead of leaving a blank line at the cell's foot. (4) A third line (b22, owner item revtex O1, interim until Flouest's contents provide the name themselves) gives article's \contentsname, \listfigurename and \listtablename, which aastex701, like revtex4-2 whose code it copies, never defines (its titles are \tocname, \lofname and \lotname, l.6657-6659), and makes its titles print them, so General's renamed contents and tocloft's titles (\cfttoctitlename is \contentsname) find them; the titles print as before unless renamed.
